t: Jean-Pierre Pury proposes Dutch East India Company settlement
c: 1714: Jean-Pierre Pury proposed a Dutch East India Company settlement of Nuyts, Leeuwin and Edels Lands.

t: King Gustav III contracts William Bolts for Swan River colony
c: 1786: King Gustav III of Sweden makes a contract with William Bolts to establish a colony at the Swan River.

t: Vancouver claims Possession Point
c: 1791: George Vancouver made formal claim at Possession Point, King George Sound, Albany.

t: Bruni d'Entrecasteaux explores southern coast
c: 1792: Frenchman Bruni d'Entrecasteaux in charge of Recherche and Espérance reached Cape Leeuwin on 5 December and explored eastward along the southern coast.

t: Baudin and Hamelin explore western coast

t: De Freycinet finds and removes de Vlamingh's plate
c: 1818: Louis de Freycinet found de Vlamingh's plate and removed it to France.

t: Dumont d'Urville visits King George Sound
c: 1826: On 26 October, Frenchman Dumont d'Urville in another ship named Astrolabe visited King George Sound before sailing along the south coast to Port Jackson.

t: Military garrison established at King George Sound
c: 1826: On 26 December, a military garrison was established on behalf of New South Wales at King George Sound with the arrival of Major Edmund Lockyer on Amity.

t: James Stirling explores Swan River area
c: 1829: James Stirling explored the Swan River area.

t: Government of Western Australia Act passed
c: 1829: The British Parliament passes the Government of Western Australia Act 1829 (10 Geo. 4. c. 22) on 14 May.

t: Area around Augusta settled
c: 1830: Area around Augusta settled.

t: First exploration over Darling Range

t: Main settlement officially named Perth
c: 1832: The main settlement is officially named Perth, after George Murray's seat in Perthshire, Scotland.

t: Western Australian Legislative Council holds first sitting
c: 1832: First sitting of the Western Australian Legislative Council, consisting of four officials appointed by Stirling to assist him in decision-making.

t: Perth Gazette, first newspaper, launched
c: 1833: On 5 January, the first newspaper, the Perth Gazette was launched.

t: Midgegooroo executed, Yagan killed near Swan River
c: 1833: Relations between the Europeans and Aboriginal people were not always amicable with many intercultural skirmishes.

t: Settlement begins in Toodyay region
c: 1836: settlement in the Toodyay region.

t: George Grey explores northwestern coasts
c: 1837–1839: George Grey explored the coasts of the North West in 1837 and Gascoyne and Murchison in 1839.

t: Edward John Eyre completes crossing of Nullarbor Plain
c: 1841: Explorer Edward John Eyre arrives in Albany walking across the Nullarbor Plain from the eastern states, with the assistance of Aboriginal guide Wylie.

t: Western Australia census records 3,842 population
c: 1843: Census recorded the population of Western Australia as 3,842.

t: John Gavin first European legally hanged
c: 1844: 15-year-old John Gavin – a child – was the first European legally hanged in the colony, for the murder of 18-year-old George Pollard.

t: Augustus Gregory surveys Greenough region
c: 1851: Augustus Gregory surveys the Greenough region near Geraldton and that area opens up to farming.

t: Francis Gregory explores Nickol Bay region
c: 1861: Francis Gregory explores the interior of the Nickol Bay region (known later as the Pilbara).

t: Telegraph line surveyed across continent
c:

t: Party leads expedition to Murchison River watershed
c: 1874: leading a party to the watershed of the Murchison River and then eastward into the Central Desert.

t: Durack family settle around Ord River, East Kimberley
c: 1883: Durack family settle around the Ord River in the East Kimberley.

t: Cyclone strikes pearling fleet at Eighty Mile Beach
c: 1887: On 22 April, a cyclone struck the pearling fleet at Eighty Mile Beach near Broome claiming 140 lives.

t: Great Southern Railway opened
c: 1889: The Great Southern Railway was opened with subsequent economic growth to the regions along the line.

t: Kings Park officially opens
c: 1895: Kings Park was officially opened on 10 August.

c: 1897: As part of the Western Australian Government's attempt to gain control of Aboriginal affairs, the Aborigines Act 1897 (61 Vict.

t: Fremantle Inner Harbour officially opens
c: 1897: Fremantle Inner Harbour was officially opened after dredging and construction under the supervision of C.

t: Premier George Leake dies in office
c: 1902: The Premier, George Leake, died suddenly on 24 June aged 45.

t: Mundaring Weir to Kalgoorlie pipeline opens
c: 1903: A pipeline from Mundaring Weir to Kalgoorlie is opened.

t: John Drayton imprisoned under parliamentary privilege
c: 1904: John Drayton is imprisoned under parliamentary privilege provisions in Western Australia for refusing to pay a fine.

t: University of Western Australia founded
c: 1911: The University of Western Australia becomes Western Australia's second tertiary institution and first university.

t: Cyclone near Port Hedland sinks Koombana
c: 1912: A cyclone crossed the coast just west of Balla Balla near Port Hedland and claimed well over 150 lives.

t: First overseas conscription referendum held
c: 1916: First of two referendums on overseas conscription in World War I.

t: Second World War I conscription referendum defeated

t: Transcontinental railway completed between Kalgoorlie and Port Augusta
c: 1917: The transcontinental railway is complete, fulfilling a promise by the Federal Government when the Colony of Western Australia voted to become a state of…

t: Prince of Wales train derailment in south-west
c: 1920: Edward, the Prince of Wales (the future King Edward VIII) was involved in a train derailment, in which his carriage overturned in the state's south west.

t: James Mitchell launches Group Settlement Scheme
c: 1921: State premier James Mitchell launches the Group Settlement Scheme in the aim of establishing a viable dairy industry in the state's south-west.

t: Edith Cowan elected to Western Australian parliament
c: 1920: Western Australia passed legislation allowing women to stand for parliament, Edith Cowan was elected to the Legislative Assembly becoming the first woman…

t: Western Australia celebrates centenary
c: 1929: Western Australia Centenary.

t: Perth telephone line connects to eastern states
c: 1930: Perth is connected to Adelaide (and subsequently the rest of the eastern states) by a telephone line.

t: Cyclone strikes Lacepede Islands near Broome
c: 1935: The Lacepede Islands near Broome were struck by a cyclone, which sank 21 pearling luggers with 141 lives lost.

t: Compulsory voting begins in state assemblies
c: 1939 – Commencement of compulsory voting in state legislative assembly elections.

t: Battle between HMAS Sydney and Kormoran
c: 1941: Battle between HMAS Sydney and the German raiding ship Kormoran off the coast near Carnarvon.

t: Japanese planes attack Broome
c: 1942: Japanese planes attack Broome.

t: Japanese occupy Christmas Island
c: 1942–1945: Japanese occupation of Christmas Island, now one of two Australian Indian Ocean Territories.

t: Pilbara strike by Aboriginal workers
c: 1946: Over 800 Aboriginal workers took part in the 1946 Pilbara strike, the first such kind of action taken by Indigenous Australians.

t: Western Australia enters Sheffield Shield competition
c: 1947: Western Australia enters the country's domestic cricket competition, the Sheffield Shield.

t: Douglas DC-4 Amana crashes near York
c: 1950: The worst civil aircraft accident in Australian history occurred when all 29 people on board the Douglas DC-4 Amana died after it crashed near York on a…

t: Operation Hurricane nuclear test at Montebello Islands
c: 1952: On 3 October the first nuclear bomb was exploded on Australian soil at the Montebello Islands, located in the north of Western Australia.

t: Aboriginal people granted full voting rights
c: 1962: Aboriginal people granted full rights to vote.

t: John Glenn passes over Perth in Mercury-Atlas 6
c: 1962: John Glenn passes over Rockingham as part of a NASA manned spaceflight mission Mercury-Atlas 6.

t: Eric Edgar Cooke last person hanged in Western Australia
c: 1964: Serial killer Eric Edgar Cooke was the last person hanged in Western Australia.

t: Donald Campbell breaks water speed record on Lake Dumbleyung
c: 1964: On 31 December, Donald Campbell broke the world water speed record in the Bluebird K7 on Lake Dumbleyung.

t: Meckering earthquake strikes Western Australia
c: 1968: On 14 October, the Meckering earthquake occurred with a moment magnitude of 6.5 and a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent).

t: MacRobertson Miller Airlines Flight 1750 crashes near Port Hedland
c: 1968: On 31 December, all 26 people on board MacRobertson Miller Airlines Flight 1750 from Perth to Port Hedland died when the aircraft, a Vickers Viscount,…

t: Indian Pacific train completes first uninterrupted journey
c: 1970: The Indian Pacific train completed its first journey by rail across the continent from Sydney to Perth.

t: Minimum voting age lowered to 18
c: 1972: Minimum voting age lowered to 18.

t: Charles Court's coalition defeats Labor government
c: 1974: Change of government.

t: NASA space station Skylab crashes in Australia
c: 1979: The NASA space station Skylab crashed in the remote south eastern part of the state.

t: Government closes Fremantle Line, replaces with buses
c: 1980: Government closes the Fremantle Line and replaces the services with buses.

t: Western Australia abolishes capital punishment
c: 1984: The Parliament of Western Australia abolished the death penalty, the last state in Australia to eradicate capital punishment.

t: Royal Commission into Western Australian government dealings
c: 1973–1993 – 19 November 1990: Labor Premier Carmen Lawrence initiates a Royal Commission into state government dealings with private businesses.

t: Joondalup railway line completed
c: 1993: The Joondalup railway line is completed to extend rail transport to Perth's northern suburbs.

t: Richard Court coalition wins election
c: 1993: Change of government.

t: Coalition loses Upper House control
c: 1996: The Liberal-National coalition loses control of the Upper House with the balance of power shifting to minority parties.

t: Western Australia apologizes to stolen generation
c: 1997: Western Australian parliament issues a formal apology to the stolen generation.

t: Geoff Gallop's Labor government elected
c: 2001: Change of government with Geoff Gallop's Labor government defeating the coalition on the back of an anti-old growth logging platform.

t: Barnett Government elected in Western Australia
c: 2008: Change of government with the election of the Barnett Government.

t: Historic ban on uranium mining reversed
c: 2008: The historic ban on uranium mining reversed.

t: Elizabeth Quay opens in Perth
c: 2016: Elizabeth Quay, a mixed-use development project in the Perth central business district opens.

t: Mark McGowan leads Labor to landslide victory
c: 2017: Change of government with Mark McGowan leading Labor to a landslide victory over the coalition.

t: Mark McGowan wins Western Australian state election
c: 2021: Mark McGowan wins state election with another landslide, said to be caused by his strong border policy.

t: Stone tools discovered at Rottnest Island
c: In 1999 Charles Dortch identified chert and calcrete flake stone tools, found at Rottnest Island, as possibly dating to at least 50,000 years ago.

t: De Vlamingh discovers and replaces Hartog's plate
c: In 1696 the plate was discovered and replaced by Willem de Vlamingh and repatriated to the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

t: William Dampier sails down western Australia coast
c: A later English visitor was William Dampier, who in 1699 sailed down some of the western coast of Australia.

t: Western Australia becomes penal colony
c: Western Australia became a penal colony in 1850.

t: John Boyle O'Reilly escapes to United States
c: In 1867 John Boyle O'Reilly, a Fenian convict, escaped on a boat to the United States, where he published a novel on the Western Australian penal system.

t: Warburton journeys from Alice Springs to Western Australian coast
c: In 1872, controversial explorer Peter Egerton Warburton made a journey from Alice Springs to the Western Australian coast.

t: Ernest Giles traverses Gibson Desert twice
c: Ernest Giles twice traversed the Gibson Desert between 1872 and 1876.

t: Gold discovered at Murchison goldfields
c: In 1891 the rush to the Murchison goldfields began when Tom Cue discovered gold at the town which now bears his name.

t: Trades and Labor Council Perth established
c: The Trades and Labor Council, Perth was established in 1891 and Perth Trades Hall opened (1912).

t: Westralian Worker newspaper first published

t: Trades Hall opens in Fremantle
c: A Trades Hall was opened in Fremantle in 1904.

t: Gold discoveries at Coolgardie and Kalgoorlie
c: Discoveries at Coolgardie (1892) and Paddy Hannan's discovery at Kalgoorlie (1893) sparked true gold fever.

t: Constitution Acts Amendment Act passed in Western Australia
c: In 1899, Forrest succeeded unilaterally passing the Constitution Acts Amendment Act 1899 63 Vict.

c: On 1 January 1901, following a proclamation by Queen Victoria, Western Australia, along with the other five British colonies of New South Wales, Queensland,…

t: Western Australia votes for secession in referendum
c: In a referendum in 1933, 68% of voters favoured secession.

t: Copper discovered at Kapunda
c: Copper was discovered at Kapunda in 1842.

t: South Australian colony faces financial bankruptcy
c: Financial bankruptcy of the colony in 1841 caused London to act.

t: South Australian Company imports Saxony merinos
c: In 1836 the South Australian Company imported pure merinos from the German region of Saxony, and cows and goats were also shipped over.
